chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Kathir, from Harun ibn Kharijah, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him),

"People hold the view that whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), it counts for him as a Hajj and an 'Umrah." He said to me: "I swear to Allah that whoever visits him, knowing his right, is forgiven for what preceded of his sins and what followed."
And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of our scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, through his chain, similarly.

key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically in the context of Ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) from a mere ritualistic equivalence to Hajj and 'Umrah, emphasizing that true recognition of his divine right (Haqq) results in the complete forgiveness of all sins, both past and future. This distinction highlights the Shia theological principle that spiritual merit is derived from gnosis (ma'rifah) and understanding the Imam's station rather than solely from physical action. The narration, transmitted through reliable chains including the narrator's father, underscores the enduring authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining the spiritual rewards of their followers.
